title: Your First Therapy Session: What to Actually Expect
description: Nervous about starting therapy? Here's exactly what happens in a first session, what to say, questions your therapist will ask, and how to prepare.

content.text: Your first therapy session can feel intimidating. What do you even say? Will you have to lie on a couch? Here's what actually happens—and how to make the most of it.
Before the Session
Paperwork
You'll likely complete intake forms covering your contact info, medical history, current symptoms, and consent for treatment. Some therapists send these ahead; others have you arrive early.
What to Bring

items: Notes on what you want to discuss

content.text: What Happens in the First Session
The First 5 Minutes
Your therapist will introduce themselves, explain confidentiality (and its limits), and help you get comfortable. You won't be asked to spill everything immediately.
Questions They'll Ask
Expect questions like:

items: 'How long have you been experiencing this?'
'What does a typical day look like?'
'What are you hoping to get from therapy?'

content.text: What You Don't Have to Do

items: Share everything in the first session

content.text: It's okay to say 'I'm not ready to talk about that yet.' A good therapist will respect your pace.
What to Say When You Don't Know What to Say
Useful phrases:

items: 'I feel anxious/sad/stuck and I'm not sure why'
'I've been dealing with [X] for a while and it's getting worse'
'I don't know if this is serious enough for therapy, but...'

content.text: Assessing the Fit
The first session is also for you to assess the therapist. Notice:

items: Does the therapist explain their approach?
Can you imagine opening up to this person?
Did they answer your questions clearly?

content.text: Research shows the therapeutic relationship—how connected you feel to your therapist—is one of the biggest predictors of success. It's okay to try a few therapists before committing.
After the Session
Your therapist may:

items: Give you something to think about or try before next time

content.text: Common First-Session Worries
'What if I cry?'
Therapists are used to tears. They have tissues. Crying is normal and often helpful.
'What if my problems aren't serious enough?'
If something is bothering you, it's worth addressing. You don't need a crisis to deserve support.
'What if I don't like them?'
Give it 2-3 sessions unless something feels very wrong. But trust your gut—if it's not a fit, it's okay to try someone else.
The Bottom Line

Your first therapy session is mostly about getting to know each other and establishing what you want to work on. There's no pressure to solve everything or share your deepest secrets. Just showing up is the hardest part—and you've already committed to that.
